lessonPlan.topic: Student Book P. 15 - A Listen and read.

details: Listen and read develops key listening and reading comprehension by helping students follow the story while hearing the correct pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, eyes on the text and accurate tracking of the words.

“Every time I go on holiday, I write a diary. It helps me remember everything I did and saw. Do you have a travel diary? Maybe we can write one together! Let’s listen to a travel story and get some ideas!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book P. 15 - B. Choose or write the correct answers.

details: Choose or write the correct answers helps students with reading comprehension, allowing them to show understanding of the text by choosing or writing  the correct answer.
Look for correct choices or written answers, clear links and understanding of the text, and neat bookwork.
“Oh no! I’ve forgotten where Kevin went. Can you be a travel detective and complete this task? What great helpers you are.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book P. 73 - A Read and choose the odd sentence.

details: Read and choose the odd sentence develops reading comprehension skills by helping students to identify incorrect sentences. It helps with careful reading and trains students to pay close attention to details.
Look for students choosing the sentence that does not match the context, careful reading, and a good understanding of the text.
“Travel detectives at the ready! Let’s read Kevin’s diary and try and spot the sneaky sentence that shouldn’t be there. Can you find it?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book P. 73 - B Read and circle T (True) or F (False).

details: Read and circle T (True) or F (False) checks students’ understanding of the text and builds comprehension, careful reading, and allows pupils to recall facts given in the text.
Look for accurate answers based on the text, a correct understanding of the story and the sentences, and clear circling of T or F.
“You’re such good detectives but do you know if something is true or false? Read the words carefully so you don’t get tricked.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book P. 73 - C Read and match.

details: Read and match lets students match words to their meanings. It supports vocabulary recall, confident decision-making and matching skills.
Look for correct matches and confidence in completing the activity.
”I just can’t remember! What does this word mean again? I bet you can help me. Let’s work together to match the words up.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book P. 16 - C Imagine you travelled to another country. Write and share.

details: Write and share develops writing and speaking by encouraging students to imagine a simple travel experience and write short details. It builds creativity, sentence accuracy, and confidence when sharing information with a partner.
Look for clear sentences in response to the writing prompts, correct spelling, and taking turns to share their work.
“Wow! We travelled to so many places together! Before we go home, let’s write about our adventures. Don’t forget to tell your partner about them. What was your favourite part?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book P. 16 - D Make your own story.

details: Make your own story develops creative writing and cultural awareness by helping students create a short story. It supports imagination, sentence building and meaningful language use.
Look for stories that show clear ideas and accurate spelling, as well as use of ideas from other countries and cultures.
“Fantastic! You are really great storytellers. Where have you always wanted to go? Create a mini travel adventure of your own and take us with you.”
